title: Bug: [Trixie] systemd-networkd.socket starts on non-smartswitch platforms
author: tirupatihemanth
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the bug

systemd-networkd.socket isn't expected to start on non-smartswitch npu/dpu platforms. However we see it tries to start and we see following errors in syslog. 

```
ERR systemd[1]: Failed to listen on systemd-networkd.socket - Network Service Netlink Socket.
WARNING systemd[1]: systemd-networkd.socket: Failed with result 'service-start-limit-hit'.
```



### Steps to Reproduce

Install Debian 13 based sonic image on non-smartswitch platform

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

### Actual Behavior
systemd-networkd.socket tries to start on non-smartswitch platforms

### Expected Behavior
We shouldn't see any errors and ideally we shouldn't start systemd-networkd.socket on non-smartswitch platforms.

### Relevant log output

```shell
root@sonic:/home/admin# systemctl status systemd-networkd.socket
× systemd-networkd.socket - Network Service Netlink Socket
     Loaded: loaded (/usr/lib/systemd/system/systemd-networkd.socket; disabled; preset: enabled)
     Active: failed (Result: service-start-limit-hit) since Thu 2025-11-13 23:33:18 UTC; 38s ago
   Duration: 1min 8.775s
 Invocation: 0fb94c68161a4024837ff54c92e7eb71
   Triggers: ● systemd-networkd.service
       Docs: man:systemd-networkd.service(8)
             man:rtnetlink(7)
     Listen: route 1361 (Netlink)

root@sonic:/home/admin# systemctl list-dependencies --reverse systemd-networkd.socket
systemd-networkd.socket
○ └─systemd-networkd.service
```

systemd-networkd.service doesn't start as expected on non-smartswitch platforms because of ExecCondition option. However we don't such such option for the socket

```
root@sonic:/home/admin# systemctl status systemd-networkd
○ systemd-networkd.service - Network Configuration
     Loaded: loaded (/usr/lib/systemd/system/systemd-networkd.service; disabled; preset: enabled)
    Drop-In: /usr/lib/systemd/system/systemd-networkd.service.d
             └─override.conf
     Active: inactive (dead) (Result: exec-condition) since Thu 2025-11-13 23:33:18 UTC; 1min 30s ago
 Invocation: 207328a3ce1d4861a43b389d393f6d37
TriggeredBy: × systemd-networkd.socket
       Docs: man:systemd-networkd.service(8)
             man:org.freedesktop.network1(5)
    Process: 25127 ExecCondition=/bin/bash /usr/local/bin/is-npu-or-dpu.sh (code=exited, status=1/FAILURE)
   FD Store: 0 (limit: 512)
```

comments.author: Staphylo
comments.body:
The file `systemd-networkd.override.conf` introduce a new `ExecCondition` to the entire `systemd-netword.service` that depends on whether there is a DPU or NPU which is an incorrect thing to do.
https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/ea0fcbf4fa89ea564ee11f47ceb080c0d830fc67/files/image_config/midplane-network/systemd-networkd.override.conf

Instead a new unit should have been introduced as a dependency of `systemd-networkd.service`
Or alternatively a new optional `ExecPre=-/some/command` via an override but IMO we should not hook into system services when possible.

comments.author: saiarcot895
comments.body:
I disagree. The `Condition*=` variables (and `ExecCondition=` in this case) are literally meant to define whether a unit should run based on the current environment of the system (whether it be the architecture of the system, whether it's running in a container/VM, or some file being missing). From the man page:

`Unit files may also include a number of Condition...= and Assert...= settings. Before the unit is started, systemd will verify that the specified conditions and asserts are true. If not, the starting of the unit will be (mostly silently) skipped (in case of conditions), or aborted with an error message (in case of asserts). Failing conditions or asserts will not result in the unit being moved into the "failed" state.`

In our case, we want to use `systemd-networkd.service` only on a DPU or NPU, but not on other systems. This would fall very well into the category of conditionally starting a service. It shouldn't matter whether it's a system service (`systemd-networkd.service` is not the only network configuration service on the system) or a regular application; systemd should treat them the same.

The issue here is the `ExecCondition=` is only available for service files; it's not available on socket files. This means whenever something or someone runs `networkctl ...` (or some subcommand that requires the use of the socket), because there's no condition saying that `systemd-networkd.socket` itself shouldn't start, it'll try to start up and eventually fail. However, what I don't understand is that something is trying to start `systemd-networkd.service` and/or `systemd-networkd.socket` very early in the boot (when `rc.local` is running), so there's some dependency chain here triggering this.

comments.author: saiarcot895
comments.body:
It _seems_ that `systemd-networkd-wait-online.service` is causing `systemd-networkd.socket` to be attempted to be started. This is because `systemd-networkd-wait-online.service` is [enabled by default](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/master/files/build_templates/sonic_debian_extension.j2#L721) for NPU/DPU purposes. This service is bound to `systemd-networkd.service`, which then tries to start `systemd-networkd.socket`. `systemd-networkd.service` is already configured to start only on a NPU or a DPU (via `ExecCondition=`), but conditions are evaluated at the time of starting the service. This means that all of the dependencies of the service will start before the condition is evaluated to be false.

One workaround here might actually be to add a dependency to `systemd-networkd.service` (and maybe `systemd-networkd.socket`) with `ExecCondition=/bin/bash /usr/local/bin/is-npu-or-dpu.sh` in the file. That way, if it is a NPU or a DPU, then it will "start" successfully; if it is not a NPU and not a DPU, then it will be treated as not meeting the conditions, and won't be considered as a failure.

comments.author: Bojun-Feng
comments.body:
I have been working on a similar dependency issue (https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/25091). I also found that `ExecCondition` is evaluated rather late during runtime. As a result, dependency chain related issues are already triggered by the time `ExecCondition` is evaluated.

The most reliable way to stop the dependency cascade seems to be masking `systemd-networkd.service` using a systemd generator. Generators run late enough to have DPU/NPU information; but also early enough to completely remove services from the dependency graph. This prevents `wait-online` or other dependents from pulling in the socket in the first place.

PR #25223 implements this generator-based masking for non-smart-switch platforms. I suspect this might resolve the socket error you are seeing as well since it cuts off the dependency chain near the source (It did remove error messages from `systemd-networkd-wait-online.service`, for more context see [#25198](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/25198#issuecomment-3812284846)).

While I recognize this involves a change to the generator, it seems to be the cleanest way to prevent the dependency cascade. Open to feedback if there is a different approach.

comments.author: saiarcot895
comments.body: That actually is better, and cleaner than having a dummy service IMO.

comments.author: Bojun-Feng
comments.body: Glad you like the approach! I have updated the PR description to track this issue as well.

linkedPullRequests.title: [systemd]: Mask systemd-networkd on non-smart-switch platforms
linkedPullRequests.author: Bojun-Feng
linkedPullRequests.body:
#### Why I did it

Fix #25091
Fix #24523

After a successful SONiC warm-reboot, the serial console prints repeated `[DEPEND] Dependency failed for systemd-networkd-persistent-storage.service` and similar messages on non-smart-switch platforms. This is a cosmetic issue that does not affect functionality but is jarring for anyone monitoring startup output.

The root cause is that `systemd-networkd.service` uses an `ExecCondition` to skip execution on non-smart-switch platforms. However, its dependent services (`systemd-networkd-persistent-storage.service`, `systemd-networkd-wait-online.service`) still attempt to start and fail with dependency errors.

#### How I did it

* Added `mask_networkd_for_non_smart_switch()` function to systemd-sonic-generator that creates a symlink to `/dev/null` for `systemd-networkd.service` when not on smart-switch platforms (DPU/NPU)
* The masking occurs at early boot during generator execution, before systemd loads unit files
* Masking systemd-networkd directly causes all dependent services to be automatically skipped by systemd's dependency resolution
* Added `validate_masked_services()` test to verify correct masking behavior across all platform configurations

#### How to verify it

1. Build a SONiC image with this change
2. Boot on a non-smart-switch platform (no DPU/DPUS in platform.json)
3. Perform a warm-reboot: `warm-reboot`
4. Monitor serial console output
5. Verify no "Dependency failed for systemd-networkd-persistent-storage.service" or similar messages appear

#### Description for the changelog

Mask systemd-networkd.service on non-smart-switch platforms to prevent dependency failure
